1.explanation: HeaderMenu.js is the component mapping over menu items and assigning href="javascript:void(0)" to disable default link behavior. HeaderMenuItem.js defines the default href for items and needs to be updated to use a safe placeholder (e.g. "#" or no href with a button role). The test files (HeaderMenu-test.js and HeaderMenuItem-test.js) and their associated snapshot files reflect the rendered output and must be updated to expect the new href (e.g. "#") instead of the javascript: URL.
1.bug_scenario: In the Carbon React UIShell HeaderMenu component, each menu item without a real link is rendered as an <a> tag with href="javascript:void(0)". React emits a console warning (and will block javascript: URLs in a future release) when it encounters that unsafe href value. Users see a red error-level warning in the console pointing at HeaderMenu.

2.explanation: HeaderMenu.js defines the default href for each <a> in the menu as "javascript:void(0)", which triggers the React warning. HeaderMenuItem.js likewise sets its default href to the same unsafe string. The two test files (and their snapshots) assert the current default href, so they will need to be updated to expect "#" (or another safe default) once the implementation changes. All six files must be edited to remove the unsafe URL and update the expected outputs in the unit tests.
2.bug_scenario: When you render a <HeaderMenu> in the React UIShell, each menu item’s link is rendered with href="javascript:void(0)" by default. React emits a warning (shown in the screenshot) that a future version will block javascript: URLs and suggests using event handlers or '#' instead. The warning is caused by the default href value in the HeaderMenu and HeaderMenuItem components.
